criteria.TP: The finding holds against the text of the requirements it cites.
criteria.BORDERLINE: Defensible but resting on one reading of an underspecified requirement, or extrapolating beyond what the requirements entail.
criteria.FP: The finding does not hold. Includes gaps whose supposedly missing requirement is present elsewhere in the collection.

format: key = C<cluster>|<category>|<index>; value = VERDICT or VERDICT|reason

verdicts.C1|gaps|1: BORDERLINE|the claim that no delivery mechanism is defined is contradicted by one of the requirements it cites, R11, which prescribes push notifications on the on-board display; the observation survives only for message format and priority.
verdicts.C1|gaps|3: FP|the payment mechanism for tolling is specified by R107 (C2), 'The system must deduct the toll cost from the online account'.
verdicts.C2|inconsistencies|4: FP|R113, R24 and R65 all state lower bounds on capacity, so they are jointly satisfiable: meeting 50.000 connections also meets 500. The requirements differ in the metric they use, which is a specification-style inconsistency, not a contradiction.
verdicts.C2|gaps|2: FP|communicating diversions to drivers is specified by R38 (C1), 'The system must immediately notify drivers in case of roadworks or diversions'.
verdicts.C5|inconsistencies|2: FP|the two requirements constrain different quantities: R55 bounds the response latency to a request, R13 the refresh interval of the data. A reply delivered within 5 seconds carrying data up to 10 seconds old satisfies both; there is no contradiction.
verdicts.C7|inconsistencies|1: FP|R63 sets a lower bound ('at least 365 days'), which retaining records without a time limit satisfies rather than contradicts; the two requirements also govern different data, critical events and vehicle movements.
verdicts.C7|gaps|1: FP|the actions the cluster is said to lack are specified elsewhere in the collection: R130 warns vehicles of obstacles, R39 and R126 alert about accidents, R46 about wrong-way vehicles, all in C1.
verdicts.C7|gaps|2: BORDERLINE|R160 (C4) does prescribe one action on stolen vehicles, refusing to respond to them; the gap survives only as the absence of a notification to law enforcement.
verdicts.C7|gaps|3: FP|tamper protection is prescribed by R29, which the finding itself cites: 'an immutable log of all decisions made by smart traffic lights for post-incident audit purposes'.
verdicts.C7|dependencies|1: BORDERLINE|the relation asserted is a shared reliance on common communication infrastructure rather than a dependency between the two requirements; neither presupposes, enables or blocks the other.
verdicts.C7|dependencies|2: BORDERLINE|the finding is hedged with 'may need'; nothing in R2 presupposes the queue count of R92.
